message.content:
Desserts come in a rainbow of hues—there isn’t a single “color of the dessert.”  
The shade you’ll see depends on the ingredients and the style of the dish. Here are some common examples:

| Dessert | Typical Color(s) | Why |
|---------|------------------|-----|
| **Chocolate cake** | Dark brown (sometimes black) | Cocoa solids give it a rich brown tone. |
| **Vanilla custard / crème brûlée** | Creamy white | Vanilla and milk create a pale, buttery hue. |
| **Strawberry shortcake** | Pink to deep red | Fresh strawberries and sometimes a pink glaze. |
| **Lemon meringue pie** | Yellow (lemon) with white meringue | Lemon curd is bright yellow; meringue is fluffy white. |
| **Red velvet cake** | Deep red | Food coloring (often beet or red cabbage) gives it a striking red. |
| **Pavlova** | White | Egg whites whipped into a crisp shell. |
| **Tiramisu** | Light brown / beige | Espresso‑soaked ladyfingers and mascarpone cream. |
| **Fruit tart** | Multicolored | Depends on the fruit used (berries, kiwi, mango, etc.). |
| **Gelato / ice cream** | Varies widely | Chocolate (brown), mint (green), pistachio (light green), strawberry (pink), etc. |

If you have a particular dessert in mind—say, a specific recipe or a dessert from a menu—let me know, and I can give you a more precise color description!
